quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This discourages car drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired, you should ride no more than:

options.text: Two hours in a day.
Four hours in a day.
Six hours in a day.
10 hours in a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Six hours in a day.
questions.explanation: Limit yourself to about six hours of riding per day to reduce fatigue. Take regular breaks on long trips.

questions.question: If a driver is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the driver.
Speed up.
Pull over to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the driver.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down. The tailgating driver may be focused on you and might not see hazards ahead that require slowing down.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Never use a staggered formation.
Place inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Not use your mirrors.
Maintain proper space between you and other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain proper space between you and other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and check your mirrors regularly. Both the lead and back riders should be experienced. Keep proper space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Decrease your following distance.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance at night. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Adjust your lane position as needed at night.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other drivers see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Move around your lane as needed to match changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, maintain a following distance of at least:

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Maintain at least four seconds of following distance under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks.
Cross the tracks at at least a 45-degree angle.
Slowly inch across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the tracks at at least a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or road seams at an angle of at least 45 degrees. Make a quick, sharp turn. Edging across slowly can catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: Maximum braking power is achieved by:

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together for maximum stopping power without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually just as powerful as car headlights.
Usually less powerful than car headlights.
Usually larger than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hand ready to use the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand ready to use the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hand ready to use the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. This is especially important when riding through areas where dangers may appear.

questions.question: What should you do when riding?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week. Regular pre-ride checks help ensure safe riding.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop
High beams on
Turn right
Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road. Signals like this help riders communicate when riding in groups.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side
The center
The right side
There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions. Choose a position that gives you more space and makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you far from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They are a good substitute for a face shield.
They are a good substitute for goggles.
They will not protect your eyes from the wind.
They protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not enough protection by itself. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind. You still need a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: When a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points upward, it means they plan to turn right or change lanes to the right. Hand signals can be used instead of or along with turn signals.

questions.question: What should you do when preparing to pass another rider on the left?

options.text: Get into the right part of the lane so they see you in their side mirror.
Get into the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center part of the lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get into the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing on the left. This improves your sight line and makes you more visible. Check your mirrors and turn your head before changing lanes.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the center portion of the lane.
Move to the left portion of the lane.
Move to the right portion of the lane.
It does not matter which portion of the lane you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane when being passed. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases the chance of a collision.

questions.question: When going through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the same part of your lane the whole time.
Stay in the left part of your lane the whole time.
Stay in the right part of your lane the whole time.
Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change all the time. Be ready to change your lane position when needed. The best path through a curve does not always match the road's curve.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shadows, and bridges—these are more likely to be slippery.

questions.question: On a long trip, what should you do?

options.text: Try to take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day and take rest breaks every two hours. Do not use caffeine or stimulants—they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. You are more likely to notice a problem by how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does it mean when the lead rider raises their left arm and points one finger, as shown in the image?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Ride in a single line.
The group will exit soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points one finger, it tells all riders to move into a single-file line.
